keyVerseText: So when even was come, the lord of the vineyard saith unto his steward, Call the labourers, and give them their hire, beginning from the last unto the first.
rootMeaning: The word ἐπίτροπος (epítropos) derives from the preposition ἐπί (epí), meaning 'over' or 'upon,' combined with the root τρόπος (tropos), related to the concept of 'turning' or 'direction,' which together imply one who is placed over something with responsibility. This etymology highlights a role of entrusted authority or oversight beyond a simple servant, emphasizing stewardship or guardianship. Unlike the English words 'steward' or 'tutor,' which can be more general, the root sense conveys a deliberate commission to manage or protect on behalf of another.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, ἐπίτροπος appears three times and is most commonly translated as 'steward' twice and 'tutors' once. This usage reveals a consistent theme of entrusted responsibility, whether managing resources or guarding a person under care. The term spans from domestic managers to guardians, indicating both administrative and protective roles. Its relatively rare occurrence underscores its significance when it does appear, marking individuals who act with delegated authority.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding ἐπίτροπος enriches our grasp of biblical stewardship and guardianship, foundational themes in Christian theology. It reminds believers that God entrusts them with responsibilities that require faithful management and protection of His gifts and people. The term also points to Christ as the ultimate steward and guardian, who administers God's kingdom with authority and care. Recognizing this role challenges Christians to embody faithful stewardship in all areas of life, reflecting God's trustworthy governance.
keyVerseReflection: In Matthew 20:8, the lord of the vineyard calls his ἐπίτροπος, or steward, to summon the laborers and distribute their wages. Here, the word underscores the steward's role as a trusted administrator who acts on behalf of the master, ensuring justice and order. This highlights the steward's responsibility not merely as a servant but as one entrusted with executing the master's will, a vivid illustration of faithful service under divine commission.
